title: Rank-first pair assembly: conditional κ = 5.102757e-5
body:
This composes PR #60's rank-first slot reclamation with PR #62's interval-strip and core-aware pair graph to improve its conditional witness:

$$
T(n)=O\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{5102757}{10^{11}}=5.102757\times10^{-5}>2^{-15}.
$$

The exponent saving is **0.0208751% above #61** (`25508460085039/500000000000000000` at `afb7cb67d1858641315cfbf4ac768ee64a8eff3a`) and **0.0208950% above #62's stacked witness** (`5101691/10^11`). The exact bit saving is `5103018/10^11`. The inherited analytic and fixed finite-alphabet multitape hypotheses remain unchanged.

## Change

Try retired slots in **descending current frame rank**, breaking ties by slot ID, on #62's interval-strip pair graph. This uses Chafik Boukhalfa's #60 compiler byte-for-byte. The previous #62 stacked witness used eumemic's #57 ascending-slot policy. The scalar graph, frame family, matching algorithm, legality checks and same-frame synthesis are unchanged.

A slot can be reused only in a containing frame, after the required span condition and explicitly paid clearing XORs. Here the new order leaves the role count unchanged but changes the physical frame paths and improves their actual fixed-basis child profile. The full compute/scatter/uncompute word is replayed on arbitrary dirty state; the extra clearing work is paid.

| Quantity | PR #62 stacked | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| h=23 auxiliary roles | 27,918 | 27,918 |
| h=25 auxiliary roles | 36,586 | 36,586 |
| Physical wires W | 137,151,806 | 137,151,806 |
| h=23 clearing XORs | 1,398 | 1,612 |
| h=25 clearing XORs | 1,827 | 2,092 |
| Bit saving | 5101952/10^11 | **5103018/10^11** |
| Conditional κ | 5101691/10^11 | **5102757/10^11** |

The actual fixed-basis block profiles retain rank **78,860,441,550**, deficit **1,846,900**, and maximum child width **529**. All 4,073,300 data pairs, copied centers, paid endpoints, the complex branch and assembly interfaces remain charged. The new result is the composition and profile witness; the rank-first rule and scalar graph retain their original authorship.

## Verification

Independent replay of both selected words passes every source, target and dirty basis vector in both orientations, reconstructs every frame transition from literal XOR incidences, and confirms exact fixed-I+J profiles with zero CRT disagreements. Exact rational checks prove all **47 assembly inequalities and seven margins**, reject both next 1e-11 grid points, and exclude #62's complete network at the new bit saving. The pinned #62 certificate is retained for comparison.

Independent reproductions of `make rank-pair-verify` pass both axes, every profile and **six focused failure controls**. Three additional h=23 orderings were screened with full word/profile checks and exact enclosures; all were worse. This is not a global optimality claim. Independent verification also replayed #62's stacked baseline.

**This PR remains ready for review.** The original construction `aa7701b68540b7863d3b66a414e4319915d6282d` passed the full local `make verify` without tracked-file drift and **29/29 [fork CI jobs](https://github.com/DominikScholz/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37821590026)**, including nine verification groups on Python 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14 and both retained formal packages. These formal jobs retain their existing scope; they do not formally prove the new full multiplication theorem.

Integration commit `ff57972b7f8c24eede3893acd843cecb5552a15c` merges current main `230b5ea8eb9344fd36f13daa2933ab7b027ce046` and resolves conflicts in CI, Makefile, contributor notices and inherited source manifests/certificates. Main's expanded verification/formal groups and reviewed community documentation are retained, with `rank-pair` added separately. **The published words, profiles, compiler, exact certificate and consumed frame/arithmetic sources remain byte-identical.** Six focused failure controls and current main's independent PR62/61 moment, child-ledger, assembly and Lean-source binding audit pass after integration. Full CI on this new integration commit remains pending. The [upstream workflow](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37826333224) is awaiting maintainer approval (`action_required`); no test jobs ran. The account has read-only upstream access. The [fork workflow for the identical integration commit](https://github.com/DominikScholz/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37826325239) is queued. This is an approval gate, not a failed test result.

```sh
make rank-pair-verify
make pair-assembly-verify
make verify
```

Construction commit: `aa7701b68540b7863d3b66a414e4319915d6282d`. The [proof](https://github.com/DominikScholz/integer-mult-bounds/blob/aa7701b68540b7863d3b66a414e4319915d6282d/research/rank-pair/PROOF.md), [exact certificate](https://github.com/DominikScholz/integer-mult-bounds/blob/aa7701b68540b7863d3b66a414e4319915d6282d/research/rank-pair/screen-certificate.json), and [compiled-word and replay receipt](https://github.com/DominikScholz/integer-mult-bounds/blob/aa7701b68540b7863d3b66a414e4319915d6282d/research/rank-pair/frame-compiler.json) are pinned to that commit. This branch incorporates the required #53/#57/#62 dependencies now merged into current main. The finite certificate does not prove the inherited all-size framed-word transfer, residual compiler, finite-alphabet tape layout, analytic, routing, prime-selection or recovery obligations.
